question: At a small extended aeration plant, what is the main purpose of activated sludge process control?
correctAnswer: Balancing solids inventory, food supply and oxygen for stable treatment
explanation: Process control balances the solids inventory with incoming food and available oxygen so the mixed liquor stays stable and treats consistently. Fixed rates or pushing solids to clarifier limits ignore changing loads.
options: Holding return sludge at a fixed rate regardless of load changes
Maximizing mixed liquor solids until the clarifier limits are reached
Balancing solids inventory, food supply and oxygen for stable treatment
Replacing biological treatment with chemical dosing during peak flows
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Activated sludge process control. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Holding return sludge at a fixed rate regardless of load changes
optionB: Maximizing mixed liquor solids until the clarifier limits are reached
optionC: Balancing solids inventory, food supply and oxygen for stable treatment
optionD: Replacing biological treatment with chemical dosing during peak flows

question: During a cold snap at a 2,400 m3/day plant, the calculated SRT has fallen to 4 days, mixed liquor is thinning, and effluent ammonia is climbing. What adjustment best addresses the cause?
correctAnswer: Reduce wasting to rebuild inventory and lengthen SRT
explanation: Reducing wasting keeps more solids in the system, rebuilding inventory and lengthening SRT so slower growing organisms are retained in cold weather. Wasting more would shorten SRT further.
options: Reduce wasting to rebuild inventory and lengthen SRT
Increase wasting to remove older solids more quickly
Cut aeration to lower the dissolved oxygen in the basin
Raise return rate sharply without changing wasting at all
sourceTitle: US EPA - Resources for Wastewater Operators
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Solids retention time management. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Reduce wasting to rebuild inventory and lengthen SRT
optionB: Increase wasting to remove older solids more quickly
optionC: Cut aeration to lower the dissolved oxygen in the basin
optionD: Raise return rate sharply without changing wasting at all

question: Influent BOD load rises sharply for several days at a municipal plant while mixed liquor volatile solids remain steady, pushing the F/M ratio above its target range. Which response best restores F/M control?
correctAnswer: Reduce wasting to build solids inventory and lower F/M
explanation: F/M rises when food increases relative to the microorganisms present, so building solids inventory by reducing wasting brings the ratio back down. Wasting more or adding load would raise F/M further.
options: Increase wasting to lower mixed liquor solids further
Stop return sludge until the basin solids wash out
Add primary effluent to raise the food supply further
Reduce wasting to build solids inventory and lower F/M
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: F/M control. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Increase wasting to lower mixed liquor solids further
optionB: Stop return sludge until the basin solids wash out
optionC: Add primary effluent to raise the food supply further
optionD: Reduce wasting to build solids inventory and lower F/M

question: An operator wastes a very large volume one day each week and none on the other days, causing MLSS and SRT to swing widely between wasting days. Which wasting strategy would smooth control?
correctAnswer: Waste smaller amounts daily toward the SRT target
explanation: Small, frequent wasting toward a set SRT target keeps MLSS and sludge age steady instead of swinging with one large weekly removal. Waiting for blanket or growth problems makes wasting reactive rather than controlled.
options: Waste only when the clarifier blanket reaches the surface
Waste smaller amounts daily toward the SRT target
Waste the full weekly volume after each heavy rainfall
Stop wasting until filamentous growth appears in the basin
sourceTitle: US EPA - Start-Up of Municipal Wastewater Treatment Facilities
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Wasting strategy. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Waste only when the clarifier blanket reaches the surface
optionB: Waste smaller amounts daily toward the SRT target
optionC: Waste the full weekly volume after each heavy rainfall
optionD: Stop wasting until filamentous growth appears in the basin

question: A plant holds dissolved oxygen near 2.2 mg/L and SRT near 12 days, yet effluent ammonia rises as basin pH falls to 6.4 and effluent alkalinity drops to about 30 mg/L as CaCO3. What is the most likely limiting factor?
correctAnswer: Low residual alkalinity limiting nitrifier activity as pH falls
explanation: Nitrification consumes alkalinity at 7.14 mg as CaCO3 per mg of ammonia nitrogen oxidized, so low residual alkalinity lets pH fall and inhibits nitrifiers. Oxygen and SRT in this case are already adequate.
options: Excess dissolved oxygen suppressing ammonia oxidizers in the basin
Short solids retention time washing nitrifiers from the system
Low residual alkalinity limiting nitrifier activity as pH falls
High mixed liquor temperature slowing ammonia oxidation rates
sourceTitle: US EPA - Resources for Wastewater Operators
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Nitrification fundamentals. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.

optionB: Short solids retention time washing nitrifiers from the system
optionC: Low residual alkalinity limiting nitrifier activity as pH falls
optionD: High mixed liquor temperature slowing ammonia oxidation rates

question: An aeration basin has a volume of 840 m3 and an MLSS of 2,500 mg/L. Waste activated sludge is removed at 14 m3/day with a solids concentration of 7,500 mg/L. Neglecting effluent solids loss, what is the SRT? Round to 1 decimal place.
formula: SRT, days = (Basin volume × MLSS) / (WAS flow × WAS solids)
